html:
The Catholic Church is the largest Christian church, with well over a billion members. It is led by the pope, the bishop of Rome, whom Catholics see as the successor of the apostle Peter.

It traces itself to the first Christians. In the Roman Empire the bishops of Rome gained special standing, and after the western empire fell the popes became great powers in Europe, ruling the Papal States in Italy for over a thousand years. The split with the Greek churches in the East-West Schism of 1054 left it the church of the Latin West. The Reformation of the 1500s took much of northern Europe away, and the church answered with the Council of Trent and new orders such as the Jesuits.

The empires of Spain and Portugal carried it across the world. Missionaries baptised peoples in the Americas, Africa and Asia, sometimes with the help of local rulers such as Afonso I of Kongo, and printed books like the Doctrina Christiana in the Philippines. The church shaped schools, art and law in these lands, and it could also silence, as when church leaders pressed Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz to stop writing.

In modern times it has fought with states, as in Mexico's Cristero War, and reformed itself at the Second Vatican Council of 1962 to 1965. Most Catholics now live in the global South. Liberation theology grew in Latin America, and in 2013 Francis became the first pope from the Americas.
sum: The Catholic Church is the largest Christian church, with well over a billion members. It is led by the pope, the bishop of Rome, whom Catholics see as the successor of the apostle Peter.
